subject: Stratus ISV: compatibility shim & roadmap asks
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@stratusisv.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: evan.cho@stratusisv.com
Date: 2027-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick sync / shim question for Redwood marketplace integration

Hi Laura and Ben,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. After circling back with engineering I wanted to surface one specific ask before the marketplace listing work: Stratus has a small legacy runtime that expects a slightly different embedding format and a 128-byte prefix header on each request. Moving the runtime is non-trivial for our customers, so we were hoping Redwood could support a short-term compatibility shim (server-side) that: 

- strips/rewrites the 128-byte prefix on inbound requests
- optionally returns a header in responses to signal shim usage

High-level questions for you:
1) Is a shim like this something Redwood Private/Dedicated can reasonably scope as a short-lived compatibility layer?
2) If so, what information would you need from Stratus engineering to estimate effort? (sample payloads, expected qps, error semantics)
3) Any security/compliance implications we should pre-clear (KMS/HSM, audit logs)?

I've attached a short matrix of endpoints and payload examples (stratus_integration_matrix_v1.xlsx). We'd like to include the shim in the initial marketplace listing to avoid blocking customers.

Appreciate your thoughts — can hop on a quick 30 if that's easier.

Best,
Maya Patel
Partnerships, StratusISV
attachments: stratus_integration_matrix_v1.xlsx
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@stratusisv.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync / shim question for Redwood marketplace integration

Thanks Maya — this is helpful context. Looping in Ben and Jonas from Partner Ops / Integrations so they can weigh in on rollout and product constraints. Initial thoughts: 

- Technically feasible: our Dedicated/Private control plane can host request pre-processing hooks. We already support request/response transforms for a handful of partners.
- Scope questions we need answered from Stratus engineering to size work:
  * exact prefix semantics (is it fixed 128 bytes or variable?),
  * whether header removal must be lossless for binary payloads,
  * QPS and peak burst estimates (esp for Dedicated pools),
  * non-functional SLAs (latency sensitivity).
- Compliance: shim changes that touch request content may need to be captured in audit logs and flagged for KMS review if any key material passes through. We'll confirm with Security.

Action items: 
1) Stratus to send sample payloads and a short traffic profile (qps/burst) — Maya, looks like you attached the matrix which helps.
2) Ben / Jonas to sketch a lightweight rollout plan (canary -> full) and a runtime configuration option (on/off per tenant).
3) I'll coordinate a short technical sync next week to align scope and timeline.

Can we target Wed 2027-09-22 for a 30-minute technical call? Please propose times.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Maya Patel <maya@stratusisv.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-22T11:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync / shim question for Redwood marketplace integration

Joining here with a practical sketch from Integrations:

Short answer: yes, we can implement a per-tenant request preprocessor that strips a fixed prefix and emits a shim header. Estimated approach and asks:

- Approach (MVP):
  1) Routing policy identifies Stratus tenant(s) by tenant ID in JWT/header.
  2) Preprocessor runs on ingress worker: if tenant flagged, strip first 128 bytes and rewrite Content-Length/metadata.
  3) Emit X-Redwood-Shim: stratus-v1 header in response for telemetry.

- Non-goals for MVP: binary streaming transforms, dynamic prefix sizes, or per-request schema validation. Those add significant complexity.

- Inputs we need from Stratus (prioritized):
  * One sample request with the 128-byte prefix (raw) and expected post-strip payload
  * Expected QPS and peak 95th percentile latency tolerance
  * A list of accounts/customers that will require the shim at launch (to scope routing and entitlements)

- Risks / compliance asks:
  * If any payloads include PII or secrets in the prefix, Security will require an architecture review and likely encrypted-at-rest handling.
  * Canary rollout must include telemetry to validate no silent failures: we prefer a staged sample (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Attached a two-page proposal (proposed-shim-approach.pdf) with an ops checklist. Proposed timeline if we get samples this week:
  - Design + security review: 1 week
  - Implementation + unit tests: 2 weeks
  - Canary + monitoring: 1 week
  => ~4 weeks to initial canary.

Maya, can you confirm sample delivery and whether Stratus prefers milestone gating (security sign-off before canary) or parallel security review?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-shim-approach.pdf

- Deliverables: attaching the raw sample and expected post-strip example (see stratus_integration_matrix_v1.xlsx). We've also uploaded a short runbook and tenant list to the Drive link in case you need it.
- Security preference: we'd like security review to run in parallel to development but sign-off gated before full rollout. That fits your proposed timeline.
- Timeline confirmation: Stratus engineering can deliver final sample payloads and traffic profiles by EOD 2027-10-05 if that works for your schedule.

Next steps: 
1) Ben / Integrations to confirm final design doc + canary telemetry (Ben to share updated doc by 2027-10-08).
2) Security teams (Redwood + Stratus) to kick off architecture review — I'll loop in our security lead Evan.
3) Schedule a short kickoff demo the week of 2027-10-11 to walk through telemetry dashboards.

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

Best,
Maya Patel
Partnerships, StratusISV
